name: Medellín
tagline: Art, hillside transit and a greener mountain escape
summary: Use Medellín as a city stay, then give Guatapé its own day. Pair Botero and the northern museums with a locally guided Comuna 13visit and time in El Poblado.
seasonNote: Comfortable highland temperatures year-round; rain can occur in any month. Allow indoor alternatives and check cable operations.
arrival: Fly to José María Córdova Airport (MDE), outside the city; arrange an authorised transfer and allow for traffic.
gettingAround: Use Metro and Metrocable for suitable daytime journeys; use an arranged taxi or reputable ride service for awkward last-mile transfers. Guatapé needs a separate road day.
cashTip: Carry small Colombian-peso notes for transport and smaller businesses; cards are useful at established restaurants.
foodTip: Try arepas and regional Antioquian dishes, then use the named vegetarian and halal-evidence filters for specific venues.
buyTip: Explore local design on Vía Primavera; ask about the maker and materials.
baseArea: El Poblado for restaurants and hotels, or Laureles for a neighbourhood stay; check walking distance to your actual Metro station.

connections.note: Approximate airborne time only; allow airport transfers and check current schedules.
Plan as a transfer day; routing and direct service vary.
Approximate airborne planning time when direct service operates; verify dates and airports.

items.name: Guatapé & Piedra del Peñol
items.summary: Spend a full day on the reservoir landscape, rock viewpoint and decorated town streets.
items.expect: A separate road excursion and a long staircase; not a Medellín walking stop.
items.tip: Check the official page before setting out.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Rating applies to Piedra del Peñol, not the entire town/day trip. Review count is not visitor footfall.

whyVisit: The climb opens a broad panorama across the reservoir’s islands and inlets.
Guatapé’s painted relief panels give the town a distinct local visual identity.
visitFlow: Leave Medellín early and visit the rock before the busiest hours.
Explore Guatapé town after the climb, then return on prearranged transport.
items.tradeoffs: Traffic and rain can extend the day; skip the climb if stairs do not suit you.
